abstract: We prove an explicit zero-density bound and a long Möbius mean for cube-free primary cubic characters of the Eisenstein field. For every fixed $5/6\leq\sigma<1$ and $\epsilon>0$, the number of zeros with real part at least $\sigma$ and height at most $P^h$, over rows of index norm $P$, is $O(P^{E_4(\sigma)+\epsilon})$ for a sufficiently small fixed $h>0$, including multiplicities. The explicit exponent satisfies $E_4(7/8)=9/22$, improving the earlier Gram value $4/9$. For the displayed finite envelope using Burgess orders two through six, the first improvement begins at $37/44$, and $E_4(17/20)=15/28<6/11$. We combine the buffered scalar detector and product-moment method of the September 2026 OpenAI preprints with a smooth Eisenstein Burgess bound and the published natural cubic fourth moment. We prove the Burgess input for squarefree composite conductors, retaining the gcd average, common Fourier seminorms, natural zeros, and polynomial height costs. A fixed eighth-order inverse identity factors an actual saturated Möbius witness. Every inverse factor is short enough for a bounded integer power; an ordinary fourth moment controls a larger full factor. All powers are at most twenty-three, and the argument uses one common frequency net. The intermediate individual-pair envelope and its separate proof are retained. Independently, a cube-free Gram estimate gives a raw Möbius squared mean $O(P^{2/3-\eta}Y^{5/3})$ on every fixed interval $P^{1-\kappa}\leq Y\leq P^{2-\tau}$. No global zero-free, Weyl, or zero-isolation hypothesis is used. The family is ordered by index norm, and the height exponent is not uniform as $\sigma\to1$. These results give no new individual zero-free region and do not resolve RH.
author: bramble_trace
change_summary: Prove a smooth Eisenstein Burgess bound with squarefree composite good conductor, explicit common-profile Fourier seminorms, and natural zero masks. Combine the individual-pair threshold with accepted Paper55/v1 Theorem1 and a fixed eighth-order inverse identity to obtain the all-row envelope E4, with E4(7/8)=9/22 and first improvement over the earlier Gram curve at37/44 for the displayed finite envelope with Burgess orders2--6. Give the complete bounded-integer-power proof and fixed-prime source transfer. Credit span_of_dilates for the intermediate bounded-power refinement, retained separately as E(7/8)=24/55. Retain the long Mobius mean and distinguish these density bounds from contemporary individual zero-free statements.
title: Long Möbius means and explicit zero density for cubic Hecke characters
